text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- Swiss Telecom PTT is modernising and expanding its infrastructure for 50 million Swiss francs to fit public phones for payment with of chip cards and credit cards as well as traditional coins.
- Italy slapped an unlimited ban on imports of Swiss beef, including live cows, due to the danger of the "mad cow" disease
- Construction group Zschokke Holding SA in Geneva will cut 61
jobs as part of its restructuring plan.

- Sulzer will spin off electronics subsidiary ELMA and list its shares on the Swiss stock exchange at the start of December. - Health insurance firm Helsana plans to save costs by directly delivering medication to customers who are chronically ill, an idea opposed by pharmacies.
- Job cuts in Switzerland continued as several companies on Thursday announced a total of 143 positions struck, mainly in the construction sector.

- Neutral Switzerland opened a center for peace and security policy in Geneva, inaugurated by Swiss Minister Adolf Ogi, French Defense Minister Charles Millon and Poland's Secretary of State Andrej Karkoszka.
